claim: Z2M's MQTT config defaults keepalive to 60 s, protocol version 4 (version 5 opt-in), and its publisher state machinery uses cache_state + cache_state_persistent + cache_state_send_on_startup — full state cached to disk and republished on startup.
stance_target: The agent should mirror the disk-backed state cache with resend-on-startup: retained MQTT messages cover broker-side state, but a local persistent state cache covers the publisher side across agent restarts.
scope_conditions: Zigbee2MQTT configuration guide (server connection + advanced behaviour)
quoted_support: # Optional: MQTT keepalive in seconds (default: 60) keepalive: 60 ... # Optional: state caching, MQTT message payload will contain all attributes, not only changed ones. # Has to be true when integrating via Home Assistant (default: true) cache_state: true ... # Optional: persist cached state, only used when cache_state: true (default: true) cache_state_persistent: true ... # Optional: send cached state on startup, only used when cache_state_persistent: true (default: true) cache_state_send_on_startup: true

claim: Z2M provides force_disable_retain as an escape hatch for brokers without retained-message support, but enabling it breaks the Home Assistant integration — retention is mandatory for HA-facing availability.
stance_target: Retained availability publishes are load-bearing for the HA integration; the jupiterOS Mosquitto fleet must keep retention enabled (and Mosquitto's retain_available default true).
scope_conditions: Zigbee2MQTT with AWS IoT Core / Azure IoT Hub class brokers vs Mosquitto
quoted_support: # Optional: Disable retain for all send messages. ONLY enable if your MQTT broker doesn't support retained message ... Enabling will break the Home Assistant integration. (default: false)
